#CSS anchor positioning

A box placed against another box, its anchor, anywhere in the document: what tooltips, menus and popovers need, without script. CSS.supports('anchor-name: --a') is true, so pages do not load a polyfill for it.

CSS
.button  { anchor-name: --menu; }
.menu    { position: absolute; position-anchor: --menu; position-area: bottom span-right;
           position-try-fallbacks: flip-block; width: anchor-size(width); }

The demo is examples/site/anchor.html, in the demos page.

#What there is
anchor-name, anchor-scopeseveral names, all; a name is looked up in the tree of the element
position-anchornormal, none, auto, match-parent, a name
anchor()in the inset properties: left right top bottom inside outside start end self-start self-end center, a percentage, a fallback, inside calc(), min()...
anchor-size()in insets, margins and sizes, with or without a name and a size, a fallback
position-areaevery keyword; normal alignment follows the area; a box too large for it stays in its containing block
justify-self, align-selfanchor-center; on an anchored box, start, end, center, stretch in what its insets leave
position-try-fallbacks@position-try rules, flip-block, flip-inline, flip-start, flip-x, flip-y, a <position-area>
position-try-ordermost-width, most-height, most-block-size, most-inline-size
position-visibilityalways, anchor-valid, anchor-visible (the initial value), no-overflow
implicit anchorsthe invoker of a popover, the anchor attribute, the originating element of ::before and ::after
CSSOMCSS.supports, element.style, getComputedStyle (the used insets of a box that uses anchors)

An anchor() on a box that is not absolutely positioned, or that finds no anchor, is its fallback, or makes the property behave as auto.

Which anchor: the last acceptable one in tree order. Under the box's containing block, an in-flow box is always acceptable, an absolutely positioned one if it comes first. Outside of the containing block, what comes first. Not the containing block itself, nothing inside the box, nothing out of an anchor-scope.

#How it works

With writing modes (docs/multicol-writing-modes.md), an anchored box is laid out once everything else is physical: start, end, the flow-relative keywords of position-area, flip-block, flip-inline, flip-start, most-block-size, justify-self and align-self take the axis and the direction they mean for the writing mode of the containing block, and the box's own for self-*; the box itself, if vertical, is an orthogonal frame root.

Style (src/style/anchor.odin): a length with anchor() or anchor-size() keeps its tree (Length_Kind.Anchor), and only on an absolutely positioned box; on another one it becomes its fallback when computed. The rules of @position-try are applied when the element's style is computed, for each option in position-try-fallbacks: they may use var() and em.

Layout (src/layout/anchor.odin): a box that uses anchors waits. layout_abs_list leaves it out and, at the end of the block layout of the pass, full or incremental, anchored_pass goes over all those boxes in tree order, since what they depend on may have moved whichever boxes were laid out again. For each one and each option it makes a copy of the box's style with the rule and the tactics applied and the functions replaced by lengths, and lays the box out with it, for the time of the call: the box keeps pointing at the record of its element, which is what incremental passes expect. The cost on a page that uses no anchor is one test of the style of each absolutely positioned box when it is laid out.

An option that does not overflow stays until it no longer fits, and until the box's style changes (Layout.anchor_last, kept across full passes).

Scrolling is not part of layout. A box follows the scroll containers around its default anchor through a space of its own (Space_Kind.Anchored), whose offset is what they add against those around the box: scrolling makes no layout, unless what was chosen depends on it (fallbacks, position-visibility, when anchor and box can scroll apart): then a change of offset makes the layout stale (Layout.anchor_stale), and the next frame or reading lays out again.

#What is missing

  • In a multi-column flow an anchor is read where it shows, as the union of its fragments, not fragment by fragment.
  • anchor-scope and names across shadow trees, by the rules of tree-scoped names: a name only matches in the tree of its element (::part() and ::slotted() rules that set it are told apart from no other).
  • The size of a scrollable containing block is its padding box, not its scrollable overflow.
  • Anchors are read where they lie at the initial scroll position, then offset: position-area rectangles that are clamped by the containing block do not change when the anchor scrolls (the "recalculation points" of the tentative tests).
  • @position-try declarations win over the element's !important ones and its animations, which should win.
  • Transitions: anchor() values interpolate when an animation asks, but the used position does not start a transition when the anchor moves. The interfaces CSSPositionTryRule and CSSPositionTryDescriptors, typed OM, the ident() function, @container anchored().
  • safe and unsafe in self-alignment are ignored (as everywhere in this engine).

Tests: src/css/anchor_test.odin, src/style/anchor_test.odin, src/layout/anchor_test.odin (with incremental layout checked against full passes), the css/css-anchor-position folder of web-platform-tests. That folder runs with a layout (the rest of the runner has none: src/tools/wpt/layout_host.odin); its reference tests are not run: the runner runs reference tests only in the folders of its REFTEST_FOLDERS (Web platform conformance), which this one is not yet.
